Rep. Maloy frames Medicaid and SNAP reforms as "reasonable," but the real issue isn't just bureaucratic trimming—it's systemic abuse. Every dollar diverted to non-citizens through ER loopholes or state-level Medicaid expansion steals resources from veterans and working Americans who funded the system.

The CBO's deficit theatrics distract from the compounding crisis: untracked usage by millions who broke immigration laws and administrative bloat. Real reform requires slashing both.

Until Congress stops treating healthcare as a global entitlement program, no spreadsheet math will fix this hemorrhage. Prioritize citizens first—then audit the waste.

The numbers and the evidence behind this crisis demand attention—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/NNnbPIAZtB

The House’s “clean CR” is just another temporary Band-Aid on a hemorrhaging budget. Continuing resolutions perpetuate D.C.’s addiction to kicking the can down the road—funding bloated bureaucracies without reform. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) proved real fiscal discipline is possible: $1.6T in cuts, structural overhauls, and prioritizing output over debt.

CRs like this one keep zombie programs alive while troops and essential services get used as political pawns. Defense spending isn’t the problem—non-defense bloat is. If Congress wants “no shutdowns,” they should pass full appropriations that slash waste permanently, not reheated 2024 budgets with accounting tricks.

Both parties love CRs because they avoid accountability. Taxpayers deserve better than endless stopgaps.
